source: Brody JS, Stemmler EJ, DuBois AB. J Clin Invest 1968;47(4):783-799. doi:10.1172/JCI105773
licence_status: PMC full text; PMC copyright notice, no CC licence seen on page. Not CC-confirmed on retrieved page; quote short excerpts only

excerpts.quote: The pulmonary arteries were responsible for 46% of total lobar vascular resistance, whereas the pulmonary capillaries and veins accounted for 34 and 20% of total lobar vascular resistance respectively.
excerpts.caveats: dog isolated lung lobes, constant flow, donor-dog blood; resistance via pressure decrease after a bolus of low-viscosity liquid; 'arteries' = lobar arterial tree to capillary

excerpts.quote: The pulmonary arteries accounted for approximately 50% of vascular resistance upstream from the sluice point when alveolar pressure exceeded venous pressure.
excerpts.caveats: same preparation; condition: alveolar pressure > venous pressure; denominator is vascular resistance upstream from the sluice point, NOT total lobar resistance (cf. 46% quote)
